claims.statement: Byron and an agent can produce diagrams together through one local DSL file.
A CLI opens a viewer, watches custom-extension files, and writes viewer edits back to those files.
Identical source and explicit rendering inputs reproduce the same geometry without hidden browser state.
Automatic layout remains useful after manual refinement and new content; avoid requiring all objects to use absolute positions.
Support nested containers and layout both within and between groups.
Tonight prioritizes file/viewer editing, durable layout tweaks, and agent edits. Richer view modes follow later.
Dragging saves a relative relationship by default; exact pinning is a separate action.
Reuse Meld syntax and refinement semantics; assess its pure compiler against the current editor engines.
Use strong defaults and minimal extra metadata; interactive and static diagrams may need distinct representations.
Reject stale viewer writes and expose invalid external edits without losing the last valid diagram or source.
The current tool is a static SolidJS app with JSON/browser persistence, layout comparison, timeline, brush, groups, and pins; it has no DSL or file server.
Follow explorEDA's file workflow and terminal authoring loop, without requiring the same grammar.
Prioritize software architecture and user flows; also support dependency-tree and call-stack diagrams.
Keep the current editor and persist its main drawing and layout edits through the DSL.
Content additions can move nearby nodes, but must preserve authored relationships and keep distant areas steady.
Tonight must persist connections, nested groups, resizing, and basic styles, alongside node moves and labels. Defer custom edge bends and label positions.
Relative placement rules may relax to obtain a clean layout. Show which preferences were relaxed and keep exact pins fixed.
Preserve comments and unrelated diagram content. Consistent whole-file formatting is expected; exact whitespace preservation is not required.

shape.appetite: Deliver the agreed DSL and two-way local editing loop tonight, October 14, 2026. This turn shapes the work; implementation has not started.
shape.problem: The current editor persists output geometry, while agent/human editing needs readable source with durable relative preferences, reproducible layout, and a safe shared file loop.

recommended_shape.summary: Adapt Meld's pure compiler into maintained TypeScript modules. Project one canonical compiled scene into the current editor; translate supported committed editor actions into source transactions. Share compiler and formatter with a local CLI.
recommended_shape.source_authority: The selected disk file, including model, recipes, relative preferences, sizes, styles, and explicit preservation anchors.
recommended_shape.render_context: One stable interactive context tonight; browser resizing changes camera fit, not compiled geometry.
recommended_shape.editor_seam: Supported source transactions -> compile -> project into current editor document. Separate user edits from projected reloads to prevent echo saves.
recommended_shape.file_seam: One localhost process owns the opened path. Watch for external replacements; use revision-checked saves and atomic file replacement. Keep unsaved proposal on conflict; no automatic merge.
recommended_shape.history: Undo/redo restores source transactions. External file replacement resets local undo. Camera, selection, previews and pending gestures are not source transactions.
recommended_shape.unsupported_actions: Disable comparison/timeline/brush Apply, manual bends, label positioning, images, and unsupported layout controls in file-backed sessions before mutation. Keep existing JSON workflow as the existing separate use case; no runtime fallback.
recommended_shape.source_edits: Formatting may normalize whitespace across the file; preserve standalone and inline comments and unrelated semantic statements.
recommended_shape.placement: Relative sibling preference by default, soft offset with explicit UI feedback when no safe sibling exists. Pins use parent-content-local coordinates. An explicit user drag can reposition a pinned object; automatic layout cannot.
recommended_shape.stability: Accepted viewer refinements write reproducible outside soft anchors, including relevant ancestors. Agent-authored additions consume these inputs without hidden geometry state. Soft preferences may relax with source-linked diagnostics. Ancestor bounds and cross-scope routes can still change, and movement must be reported.

success_moves: Reuse the current editor shell and gestures, and adapt the existing pure Meld compiler; avoid building another editor or adding a new layout dependency.
Use source transactions as the only durable file-backed commit. Keep reload projection, previews, camera changes, and writer echoes outside that commit path.
Prove nested relative placement, group resize, pins, source comments, and external additions in one actual file before expanding editing coverage.
Use explicit source anchors for stability; compare world and parent-local positions so ancestor movement cannot masquerade as a stable region.
Exercise a real temporary file and localhost watcher with intentional stale saves and invalid source. No cloud, database, provider credentials, or emulator is required.
Disable unsupported file-backed actions and retain the existing JSON workflow separately; an unsupported change must never look saved.

first_proof.question: Can the existing editor show and save a source-compiled nested diagram, preserving relative intent, exact pins, source comments, and reproducible geometry after an external addition and restart?
first_proof.artifact: One temporary .meld architecture fixture, a running local file session, before/after source and canonical geometry records from Node and the actual browser editor.
first_proof.decision_rule: Pass only if drag creates a readable relative preference; group resize and explicit pin persist; an external connected-node addition is visible; unrelated distant anchors stay within declared solver precision when feasible; impossible movement is diagnosed; source comments/content survive; restart matches saved canonical nodes and routes. On failure, repair the compiler/editor seam before more tools. Do not replace the editor or silently drop accepted scope.
first_proof.scope: One nested group with siblings, one root-level distant region, one exact pin, one connection, one comment. Add a sibling externally after a viewer save.
first_proof.dependency_role: Real local filesystem and localhost transport; recovered compiler adapted behind one narrow projection seam. Browser integration is real; no fake DOM proof substitutes for a drag.

reuse_evidence.meld: Parser, sibling-scoped relative preferences, stays, pins, sizes, nested layout, and pure geometry already exist in reference/meld/original/src/meld-core.js. No new dependency is required to examine them.
reuse_evidence.editor: remember/change are committed geometry transaction paths; finishDrag records direct gestures; undo/redo restore normalized document snapshots. setDocument calls change and would echo a file reload without an explicit projection path.
collisions: Current normalize does not preserve arbitrary DSL fields: keep source/session state outside the derived document.
Editor geometry is world-based; Meld pins/stays are parent-local. Group movement and reparenting need explicit conversion.
Meld group dimensions are minimum layout bounds, not the current editor's frame semantics. Requested sizes must respect children and show resulting bounds.
Meld node kinds use card geometry and a narrower palette. Add only the agreed editor shapes/colors/sizes without silently losing source data.
Current editor reroutes independently. Ensure visible route geometry and CLI geometry use one canonical routing result or shared deterministic routing path.
Meld reports unsatisfied required rules, but lacks complete soft-preference relaxation diagnostics. Add residual checks tied to source rules.
Meld's line-replacement helper can discard inline comments. It is a reference, not a ready comment-preserving formatter.
Meld's saved stays alone do not guarantee all distant world geometry remains unchanged, especially after container growth. Test ancestry and report movement rather than promise absolute locality.
Current editor snapshots cannot serve as complete undo entries for relative intent; source transactions must own file-backed history.

history.change: Created planned initiative. Recovered original Pro conversation, all 31 ZIP files, and three notebook photos. Inspected current editor and explorEDA CLI/file adapter. User selected the core authoring loop for tonight and relative placement as the default drag behavior.

Completed six intent questions in two rounds. Kept current editor; prioritized architecture and flows, local movement, bounded saved edits, soft relative rules with fixed pins, and preservation of unrelated source text.

Updated intent brief after six questions. Latest correction permits and expects automatic whole-file formatting; preserve comments and unrelated diagram content. No shape or plan exists to invalidate.

Shaped tonight's file-backed DSL loop. Recommend adapting Meld compiler into current editor, one source transaction authority, revision-checked local writes, bounded editing coverage, and explicit soft-rule diagnostics. Isolated compiler instances produced equal canonical geometry for one nested fixture; a root pin stayed at local x=900 after adding a sibling. This was not browser integration, fresh-process, route-projection, distant-anchor, or end-to-end proof.

User asked to execute the shape as stacked PRs. Moved docs and Meld reference into the main checkout and rebased the plan onto the typed SolidJS app (cleanup/normal-app); the commit/restoreDocument seam replaces the older editor.js remember/change seam. Created the implementation plan with four milestones and set the initiative active.

Implemented all four milestones as stacked branches. First-proof evaluation passed: Meld compiler adapted into the existing editor without replacing it; Node/browser geometry equal at every step of pnpm prove:file (19/19). Changes from the shape: root scope no longer clamps to nonnegative coordinates (it pushed anchors aside); new objects default to color=auto; resizes never write move preferences. Arrow-key nudges need canvas focus (existing behaviour), so the proof uses P for its save race.

Pushed to byronwall/draftably. Merged remote main (release setup) into cleanup/normal-app and carried it up the stack; opened #3 (base rebuild) and stacked #4–#7. pnpm prove:file still 19/19 after the merge.

questions.question: What diagrams define the first successful version?
questions.answer: Software architecture and user flows are the most important starts. Dependency trees and call stacks also matter.
questions.effect: Prioritize architecture and flow examples; include tree and call-stack use cases without assuming separate notation engines.

questions.question: How much of the current Diagram Studio must work through the DSL tonight?
questions.answer: Keep the current editor; make its main drawing and layout edits persist.
questions.effect: Retain the editor; assess a bounded set of persistent main edits rather than replacing it or requiring every advanced tool tonight.

questions.question: How much movement is acceptable after an agent adds a connected node?
questions.answer: Nearby nodes can move; preserve saved relationships and keep distant areas steady.
questions.effect: Treat local edit stability as a product requirement separate from deterministic replay.

rounds.theme: Saved edits, conflicting rules, and source preservation

questions.question: Which visual edits beyond node moves and labels must persist tonight?
questions.answer: Connections, nested groups, resizing, and basic styles; defer custom edge bends and label positions.
questions.effect: Bound tonight's source-backed editor operations; defer manual edge bends and label placement.

questions.question: What happens if a saved placement rule prevents clean layout?
questions.answer: Relax relative placement rules when needed, show what changed, and keep exact pins fixed.
questions.effect: Relative rules are soft preferences with visible relaxation feedback; exact pins remain hard constraints.

questions.question: Should viewer saves preserve comments and formatting?
questions.answer: Preserve comments and unrelated text; change only affected statements.
questions.effect: Require targeted source edits rather than full-file serialization.
